frequency_question: How often have similar trade or regulatory actions successfully completed all mandatory procedural and administrative steps within 129 days or fewer?
membership_rule: Includes executive orders, tariff proclamations, and major federal administrative actions under statutory trade authorities where the implementation window was under 130 days from announcement to effective date.

cases.name: 1971 Nixon 10 percent import surcharge (IEEPA precursor / Tariff Act)
2018 Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs (announced March, effective March/June)
1987 sanctions/tariffs on Japanese electronics under Section 301

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named rapid executive trade tariff implementations; historical population of emergency tariff actions is small but uniformly rapid when statutory authority is invoked directly.
known_gaps: Excludes standard multi-year negotiated trade agreements (like USMCA updates) which follow a statutory congressional consultation timeline exceeding 129 days, but those are excluded by the premise of unilateral executive implementation.
skeleton: Executive actions utilizing emergency or statutory tariff powers (Section 232, Section 301, or IEEPA) bypass standard notice-and-comment APA delays, allowing direct publication and customs integration.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 4 documented rapid executive trade actions within the window
validity_reason: Valid for the duration of the current presidential administrative authorities and statutory frameworks governing emergency trade actions.
